name: OpenWorld, Inc. (formerly VerifyMe, Inc.; now trades as OPNW)

profile.description: TICKER CHANGE: VerifyMe, Inc. (VRME) completed a reverse merger with Open World Ltd. effective October 1, 2026. It renamed itself OpenWorld, Inc. and now trades on the Nasdaq Capital Market as OPNW, so the VRME symbol no longer trades. Legacy OpenWorld holders own about 85-90% of the combined company and legacy VerifyMe holders about 10%. VerifyMe did a 1-for-10 reverse split on September 29, 2026 and paid a $1.50 special cash dividend around closing. OpenWorld, based in Camana Bay in the Cayman Islands, describes itself as a digital-assets and blockchain company offering real-world-asset tokenization, stablecoin infrastructure, capital-markets advisory and governance structuring for clients in the Gulf, Europe, Australia and Southeast Asia. Matthew Shaw is Chairman and CEO. The legacy VerifyMe brand-protection and PeriShip precision-logistics business was shrinking fast before the merger: Q1 2026 revenue was $1.77M versus $4.46M a year earlier. OPNW shares fell from $5.54 on their first trading day to $0.92 by October 30, 2026.

innovation.label: WEAK
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): The legacy VerifyMe pivot into precision logistics (PeriShip) has not held up. Revenue fell from $25.3M in 2023 to $16.4M in 2025, and Q1 2026 revenue dropped 60% to $1.77M [2][3]. The October 2026 reverse merger into tokenization is a wholesale change of business, not yet a proven launch, so it earns one point at most [1][4]. AI Deployment (1/2): OpenWorld announced a proposed acquisition of Blocksight on October 1, 2026, billed as 'agentic tokenization infrastructure', and signed a definitive agreement on October 18. No AI product is shipping and no AI savings have been reported [5]. Market Share (0/2): OpenWorld is a sub-scale entrant (about $12M market cap) in a crowded RWA-tokenization field and has no measurable share [2]. Pipeline (1/2): Named initiatives include tokenized OPNW shares on Figure's OPEN network (targeted for Q4 2026), the Blocksight deal and an October 7 term sheet for a structured IP-backed transaction of up to $130M with BeyondAI. None comes with revenue visibility [5][6]. R&D Intensity (0/1): No R&D disclosure is available for the combined company.

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (1/4): OpenWorld's only stated purpose is to 'co-architect enterprise blockchain initiatives alongside governments and institutional partners'. That is boilerplate for the digital-assets sector, with no deeper cause or execution record (the company was founded in 2023) [4]. Community Impact (0/2): No charitable or community programs were found. Employee Retention (0/2): The board and executive team were completely reconstituted at closing, and no retention data exists for the combined company [1]. Insider Buying (0/2): No open-market insider purchases were found. About 76% of post-merger shares are under a 180-day lock-up rather than being bought by insiders [1].

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: LIQUIDITY FLOOR TRIGGERED, so Infrastructure = 0. OPNW's average volume of 309,762 shares at $0.9152 is about $283K of daily traded value, below the $1M minimum [2]. Even apart from the floor, the last reported trailing figures (legacy VerifyMe) are poor. ROE is -42.8%, profit margin -47.1% and revenue growth -57.8% YoY, offset only by low leverage (D/E 7.5%) [2]. Forward P/E and PEG are set to null because the provider's forward P/E of 224.5 was computed on the pre-merger VRME price and share base, and no post-merger estimates exist. The five-year revenue CAGR is also null because the combined entity's historical revenue is not comparable.

ai_resilience.label: HIGH RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (4/9): OpenWorld's revenue lines are capital-markets advisory, governance structuring, public-markets strategy and tokenization structuring. These are knowledge services, and AI agents and automated smart-contract tooling are already compressing them [4][5]. OpenWorld's own Blocksight deal is framed as 'agentic tokenization', which concedes that automation is reshaping the workflow [5]. The legacy logistics-analytics dashboards (PeriTrack) are also easy for AI to replicate. The rating is EXPOSED rather than VULNERABLE only because regulatory structuring in Gulf jurisdictions still needs human relationships. AI Opportunity (0/1): No AI revenue has been reported.

infinite_game.summary: This is a finite-game situation. A shrinking legacy company (VerifyMe) served as the Nasdaq listing vehicle for a two-year-old tokenization startup. The combined company replaced its leadership and paid out a special dividend, and the shares fell about 83% in its first month. Through Sinek's lens, nothing here yet shows a cause that people would sacrifice for or a team built to endure.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): OpenWorld presents itself as building blockchain infrastructure with governments, such as its Saudi Arabia RWA Tokenization Center of Excellence tied to Vision 2030 [4][6]. The aim reads as marketing language, is interchangeable with many digital-asset firms and has no record of shaping costly decisions.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): The merger brought complete organizational upheaval. Legacy VerifyMe leadership was replaced, the board was reconstituted under Matthew Shaw, and the legacy business's revenue collapse implies deep cuts. Nothing suggests a circle of safety [1][3].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Messaging centers on claims of being a 'leading tokenization platform', with no acknowledgment of established players such as Figure, Securitize or the major custodians as benchmarks to learn from. Figure appears only as a partner [6].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (0/2): The VerifyMe-to-OpenWorld change is a dramatic shift, but Sinek's test requires a pivot driven by the Just Cause. This one followed the legacy business's 60% revenue collapse, used the listed shell as a vehicle and handed about 90% ownership to the incoming company [1][3]. It is a change of control, not a reinvention.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (0/2): Instead of reinvesting through the downturn, the company paid a $1.50 special cash dividend at closing and set up a $50M GEM equity line that carries a $1.0M commitment fee. Both are financing moves rather than long-term capability bets [1][7].

investment_thesis: The bull case is purely optionality. OpenWorld enters public markets with a Nasdaq listing, about 13.4M shares outstanding and a roughly $12M market cap [1][2]. It has a visible pipeline: tokenized shares on Figure's OPEN network targeted for Q4 2026, a definitive agreement to acquire Blocksight, a BeyondAI term sheet for a structured IP-backed transaction of up to $130M, and a Saudi RWA tokenization center tied to Vision 2030 [5][6]. If even one large institutional tokenization mandate converts to recurring fees, revenue could re-rate meaningfully against such a small base.
thesis_continued: The bear case dominates. This is a reverse merger into a pre-revenue-scale digital-assets startup, and the VRME ticker no longer exists. The legacy VerifyMe business was collapsing, with Q1 2026 revenue down 60% to $1.77M and 2025 revenue of $16.4M down from $25.3M in 2023 [2][3]. OPNW fell from $5.54 on October 1 to $0.92 on October 30, 2026, and at about $283K of daily traded value it fails IOWN's $1M liquidity floor [2]. The $50M GEM equity line points to ongoing dilution, about 76% of shares come out of lock-up in tranches through day 180, and Nasdaq continued-listing compliance is an explicit risk in the S-4 [1][7]. The stock is not investable for IOWN.
key_catalysts: Go-live of tokenized OPNW shares on Figure's OPEN network, targeted for Q4 2026 [6]
Closing of the Blocksight acquisition (definitive agreement signed October 18, 2026) and conversion of the up-to-$130M BeyondAI IP-backed transaction term sheet into a fee-generating mandate [5]
First combined-company quarterly report showing whether OpenWorld's advisory and tokenization revenue offsets the collapse of the legacy logistics business [3]
key_risks: Liquidity and listing risk: about $283K of daily traded value and a price below $1 after an 83% first-month decline put Nasdaq minimum-bid compliance at risk, which the S-4 explicitly flagged [1][2]
Dilution from the $50M GEM equity facility plus release of about 76% of post-merger shares from lock-up in tranches through day 180 [1][7]
Business-model risk: the RWA tokenization and stablecoin market is early, regulation-dependent and crowded, and OpenWorld has no disclosed recurring revenue base [4][5]
